prompt: Finding the 3 nearest stored vectors to a query vector, stored in a plain SQLite table:

options.label: Without sqlite-vec
options.content: Vectors are stored as serialized blobs in an ordinary column. Your application pulls every row back out of the database, deserializes each blob, and computes cosine similarity itself in a loop, then sorts the results in your own code. It works, but every part of the actual comparison logic lives outside SQL, in whatever language your app is written in.

options.label: With sqlite-vec
options.content: Vectors live in a real vec0 virtual table. A single query - something like SELECT * FROM chunks WHERE embedding MATCH ? ORDER BY distance LIMIT 3 - does the entire nearest-neighbor search inside the database engine itself, right alongside ordinary WHERE clauses on other columns. No separate service, no custom comparison loop - just one more thing expressed in SQL.
